ab_title: About the Data — How visafreely Verifies Visa Requirements
ab_desc: Where visafreely's visa data comes from, how pairs are verified against official sources, and what the 'Last verified' stamp does and does not promise.
ab_lede: Visa information is only useful if you can tell how fresh it is. This page explains exactly where our data comes from and how it is checked.
ab_stamps_p: Every pair page on this site carries one of two stamps, directly under the answer. There is no third state, and no answer hides which one it has.
ab_seal_v_a: Verified — last checked {date} against an official source:
ab_live1_b: . The date is the day the check was completed; the source is named and linked, so you can re-check it yourself.
ab_live2_b: . The dashed stamp is not an apology — it is the pair's place in the verification queue, stated on the page instead of hidden.
ab_seal2_a: Data from the passport-index dataset, {vintage} snapshot
ab_seal2_override: — with a correction applied by visafreely (see the changelog)
ab_seal2_b: . This pair has not yet been individually verified against an official source; see
ab_changed2: This value was last changed on {date}.
ab_how1_d: The foreign ministry, immigration authority or official embassy page for the route — never another visa site.
ab_how2_d: Compare the dataset value against that source: the requirement itself and the permitted stay.
ab_how3_d: Record the check date and the source on the pair page. If the source disagrees with the dataset, the value is corrected first.
ab_how4_b: — old value, new value, date and official source.
ab_base_a: The starting point is the open
ab_base_b: (MIT licence), which maps the visa requirement for every passport → destination pair: visa free (with the permitted stay), visa on arrival, e-Visa, electronic travel authorisation, visa required, or no admission. We use the February 2026 snapshot as the base layer for all {pairs} pairs.
ab_base_p2: A snapshot is a photograph, not a feed — visa rules change every month, and the snapshot is already wrong in places the day it is taken. So the snapshot is never the final word on this site.
ab_layer_a: We check pairs individually against primary official sources — foreign ministries, immigration authorities and official embassy pages — starting with the most-travelled routes, and record the date and the source for every check. A pair page shows a
ab_layer_b: date only when such a check has actually been completed for that pair. Pairs not yet checked say so plainly and show the dataset's vintage instead. At launch, {verified} pairs carry a verified stamp; the rest are queued in a published order of travel importance.
ab_layer2_a: When a check finds the dataset is wrong, we correct it and publish the change — old value, new value, date and official source — in the
ab_layer2_b: . Some rules carry an announced end date (temporary visa-free policies are common); where an official source gives one, the pair page shows it as a scheduled change.
ab_promise_h2: What the stamp does not promise
ab_promise_p: “Last verified” means the requirement matched the named official source on that date. It does not guarantee entry: border officers decide admission, rules can change between the check and your trip, and pages here cover ordinary passports on short tourist visits — not work, study, residence or special passport categories. Always confirm with the destination's embassy or official immigration authority before travelling, especially if your trip depends on it.
ab_corr_p: Found something that disagrees with an official source? That is exactly the feedback the changelog runs on — every confirmed discrepancy becomes a correction entry with its source attached.
ab_widget_h2: Put the checker on your own site
ab_widget_a: Run a travel blog or site? The same checker that powers our home page is available as a free embeddable widget — one iframe, no signup, and it stays current with the data here. See
fb_li1_b: — {count} passports against {count} destinations. Every pair carries one status (visa free, visa on arrival, e-Visa, ETA, visa required or no admission) and a maximum stay where the rule sets one.
fb_ways_h2: Three ways to work with us
fb_card3_b: is free to embed, and it stays free. The one condition is the attribution inside it — the “Powered by VisaFreely” line and its link must stay in place. If you need the checker without attribution, or as part of a product you sell, that is a commercial arrangement: ask below.
fb_same_p1: The public site. Answers stay free and complete for individual travellers, and every route page keeps the official government application route next to any paid option. Licensing is only about reuse inside other products — nothing here puts traveller answers behind a paywall.
fb_same_p2: And the warning we give travellers applies under any licence too: this data is a guide, not an official source. Requirements change, and the destination's embassy or immigration authority is the final word.
